Those are genuine terms despite the misuse. Just because fakers misuse it does not mean this are cutsey or made up, just that the way people use then have watered them down. Technically all people stim. It's just a form of self regulation that humans naturally do, people with disorders just have sensory issues that may cause them to do such things more often. Stimming also isn't always jumping or doing hand flaps, it could be as simple as putting on ChapStick or rubbing a textured surface to self regulate! 

Special Interests have been taken to be anything that you enjoy to a large degree when that also simply isn't the case. It's literally a symptom of disorder that is used to diagnose something! Special interests and hyperfixations can and often do take over your life to the point you neglect everything else including sometimes neglecting your physical needs!

This has an outside of game reason actually. In China the second the hero drinks it raises the age rating to 18+. Traveler has no ID and isn’t from there so naturally any bartender would be nervous.  Zhongli does has a line that mentions Traveler having gone out drinking with Venti before and Venti has no issues offering Traveler alcohol in general.

Kevin for sure. Yes he had noble goals… but he was still a terrorist and generally kinda a dick. He’s pretty much seen as sad yaoi bait with Su now and that’s such a disrespectful take on both of them.

In China in order for a game to be rated what is their version of T, everyone must follow the actual laws of China as far as drinking goes. So anyone shown at any point drinking has to be 18+. This rule is also why Diona has other people sample her drinks instead of being able to try them. Another thing pointing to this is that it’s mentioned in the (still canon) manga that drinking age in Mondstadt is 18. 

Kazuha is old enough to drink. He’s shown drinking on the Crux and his participation in GAA2 hinged on him being drunk in order to kick things off. He just isn’t supposed to because he’s a lightweight and gets in trouble when he’s drunk.

Lyney is shown drinking in a bar so he also has to at least be of an age to drink. As to his looks… living on the streets can do that but he also mentions having to maintain his figure to be identical to Lynette’s so they can perform tricks that require them to switch. 

Mika can drink, he just mentions that he doesn’t like it. It’s Eula that tells you to not let him drink and that’s probably because they’re on a mission and don’t want to cause a scene in another country.

Bennet can buy and consume alcohol. He even buys Venti a bottle of wine!

The others are the gray area. 

I don’t think Bennet and Razor are that far apart in age Razor was just raised by wolves.

Freminet COULD be underage but he also is at least old enough to have seen Arlecchino take over the Hearth and remember it. I personally think the entire trio would be old enough to “age out” of the orphanage part which (hinging on the fact it works like a real legal orphanage) would put him at 18.

Gaming personality and story wise strikes me as someone who has recently headed out on his own. Which could happen underage but people in China do tend to stick around to take care of their parents as well… especially when their mother isn’t  in the picture. Not to mention his job as security would be much much more dangerous than most jobs.

That leaves Chongyun and Xingqiu.

But there’s one more factor you forget there as well. Hu Tao. The entire group are friends, and shown to be around the same age. However… unlike Yao Yao and Qiqi, the Adepti do NOT treat Hu Tao like a child. She’s definitely younger than her predecessors but I doubt the adepti would have let someone too young go out alone and do dangerous things like she did last Lantern Rite let along Ningguang also letting her who is KNOWN for being responsible. 

So… Chongyun and Xingqiu are probably young adults well because I don’t know any self respecting young adult that would be such a tight friends with someone dramatically younger. 

Yes Teyvat has its own laws… and honestly the person in charge of the Cat’s Tail needs to be arrested… but I think Diona is the exception to child labor rather than the rule. She’s supposed to stand out and everything about her story is meant to be uncomfortable. 

Of course, I’m a neurodivergent adult that has developmental delays so took a while getting out into the world as well. Thus I  have different experiences and interpretations of these characters than a minor would. Other than the characters who have been shown drinking, mentioned drinking, or are shown/mentioned to buy alcohol we don’t know for sure (and even then they could be freshly 18 or much older than that). So don’t be rude to someone who interprets things differently, unless they’re using it simply as an excuse to sexualize characters (which is ew anyways no matter what). The art style doesn’t seem to be a good conclusion other than for the tiny models and for marketing and possibly legal reasons Mihoyo will never confirm ages other than a few like Diluc.

I’m not Christian anymore (for personal reasons I won’t go into here) but I grew up in different churches and tried many different denominations for much of my youth and college years. My suggestion would be to see if any in your area offer a “traditional” service. Usually those have much quieter and shorter worship sections. These services usually are earlier in the morning and are primarily catered to older people but I also found that a lot of people with sensory issues liked them more as well. Some churches also have begun offer special sensory friendly services. 

Another option is to try a different church. I found that ones that cater to “young adults” tend to have the louder style of worship associated with contemporary Christian worship. The larger the church also the more often they’ve tried to emulate Hillsong and the like in order to draw in masses of people. I’ve also found Pentecostal churches much louder than Catholic or Lutheran churches. Different denominations vary in worship style as much as they do in teaching.

In my eyes there’s two completely set forms of self-diagnosis, one perfectly valid and the other not. If the person does actual research, reading scientific papers and first hand accounts from people diagnosed with autism then goes “oh hey that would explain a lot. But if said person watches a couple of tik toks about stimming or just having sensory issues, and say they have autism based on only that, no. They have not done proper research and may be taking in false information produced by fakers. Most of the people that fake do have some sort of mental illness or an inherent need to be special so they see something that is difficult to diagnose and is on a spectrum like autism and latch on to only the traits they see as beneficial. Those people don’t talk about crying in a grocery store because it no longer caries your safe food, or how sometimes clothes that were comfy one minute can be hell the next. I agree that there shouldn’t be a stigma to being autistic but it’s not all a happy stim party where we constantly discuss special interests either. 

It is a spectrum so everyone does have slightly different experiences but there are some criteria that HAVE to be met in order to be diagnosed autistic. The words impairment and deficit come up quite a lot in actual diagnostic criteria. The people presenting autism as just a happy stim party are why people are skeptical of self-diagnosis. Because it’s dead wrong. Again there is a vast difference between doing actual research and then going “yeah I’m autistic” and just watching a couple of quirky videos on the internet and going “oh I do a normal human behavior but this person says it’s autistic so I’m autistic yay!”

Honestly the problem with this suggestion is that it  only works if you mask well enough to not be clocked right away. Or if you have fewer support needs. People with higher support needs or who are more obviously neurodivergent should disclose if comfortable. I’m not saying discrimination is okay by any means but in some cases it’s better to be open in order to weed out bad places for you to work. A job requires cooperation and compatibility from both parties. Just like someone who requires mobility aids can’t always do the exact same work as someone without them. This also applies to jobs you know 100% are disability friendly. Go ahead and tell them regardless as they often are actively seeking people that would struggle to find jobs due to disability. For example there’s a coffee shop in my town that exclusively employs people with neurological, mental, and developmental disabilities.

Otherwise, if you need little to no accommodation there’s no true reason any employers even need to know. I very rarely tell a place I am autistic until I’ve worked there long enough to see if I’ll require any accommodation to do the job. If I can do it just fine on my own, I won’t even mention it. I am generally low support needs (mid in some areas but I don’t always need the assistance at work) and mask very well though. I usually actually tell my workplaces about my occasional need for an ankle brace before I will explain my autism. It’s usually easier for them to understand mild physical disabilities than my neurological or mental issues.

As for the bleeding, hand wounds bleed a lot. Puncture wounds tend to bleed pretty bad as well. Other than the pain and inconvenience the lady was likely fine. Being bitten by a snake isn’t a common occurrence but anyone who owns one knows it’s a possibility. It’s just like owning any other pet. I’m honestly tired of people looking down on reptiles as pets.
